description:
The configuration reference becomes the single adopter-facing home for the issue artifact directory convention and the development-area classification, and the other adopter documents that restate either fact become pointers to it.

## Background

The configuration reference is already the strongest anchor: it owns the documentation configuration keys, the move-versus-copy semantics, and the three-state policy status, and it already disclaims its own example as illustration rather than vocabulary. What it lacks is the path convention, which currently appears only in a how-to, and a statement of the area classification as a classification rather than as an example list.

Several other adopter documents carry partial copies: an example configuration file, a glossary, a command reference, a planning-bracket how-to, and the project readme. Each keeps whatever is genuinely its own — command mechanics belong to the command reference — and cites the canonical home for the rest.

Where a fact has one source of truth, prose reaches it by citation rather than by a hand-maintained copy, and a duplicated list is a staleness defect rather than a convenience.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The configuration reference states the issue artifact directory convention, including how the directory name is derived and that filenames inside it carry no short-id prefix.
- [hard] REQ-02: The configuration reference states the development-area classification as the canonical statement of which areas are managed and which are permanent.
- [hard] REQ-03: The configuration reference names the command that resolves an issue's canonical artifact directory as the way to obtain the path.
- [hard] REQ-04: Other adopter-facing documents that previously restated either fact cite the canonical home instead.
- [hard] REQ-05: Repository-local examples are identified as this project's configuration rather than as the shipped default.
- [hard] REQ-06: Mechanical documentation checks over the adopter surface pass.
title: State the artifact layout facts in one adopter reference
